name: Should I choose grab bars or blocking during the remodel?

mainEntity.name: Is it better to install grab bars now or add blocking behind the walls for future grab bars later?
mainEntity.text: Is it better to install grab bars now or add blocking behind the walls for future grab bars later?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the walls are open, adding blocking is usually a low-cost way to future-proof the bathroom. Blocking provides solid backing for grab bars, shower seats, and other accessories later without requiring another demolition project. In an active accessible remodel, visible grab bars can be installed immediately in the shower, near the toilet, and at transfer points, but hidden blocking gives flexibility if the user’s needs change over time. This is especially useful in aging-in-place projects where mobility can change gradually. A good contractor will place blocking at the correct heights and locations before tile goes up, since retrofitting after the fact is more expensive and disruptive. Homeowners should also confirm that the wall structure can support the load and that the final finish layout does not interfere with bar placement.
acceptedAnswer.description: Adding blocking during the remodel is usually the smarter choice because it lets grab bars be installed securely now or later without opening the walls again. For safety and flexibility, many accessible remodels include blocking at the shower, toilet, and tub area even if bars are not installed everywhere immediately.
